title: Covington's Nursery: more than 50 years of growing Rowlett
excerpt: Rowlett neighbors say the family-run nursery is a community staple – friendly staff, and always another event that gives back.
coverAlt: The Covington's Nursery team in yellow shirts, waving in front of the herbs and veggies greenhouse
body:
When we asked Rowlett who they're thankful for this year, one of the first answers was a place many of us have been visiting for decades: Covington's Nursery.

High school sweethearts Joe and Gayle Covington opened the nursery more than 50 years ago, back in 1972. Today it's an 18-acre destination on President George Bush Highway, with greenhouses full of plants, a landscape design team, and staff who will happily tell you what will actually survive a North Texas summer.

But what neighbors talk about most is how often Covington's shows up for the community. Rowlett resident Andrew Balettie, who nominated them, put it this way: "Their staff is always friendly and well trained, and it seems like every time I turn around they are hosting another event for the benefit of the community, like their recent blood drive or fall festival. We love spending our money locally at Covington's!"

The fall festival has been a Rowlett tradition for years, with a hay maze, pumpkins and activities for kids. In past years, admission was a canned good for the Rowlett Needy Children's Fund.

So the next time you need a tree, a flat of pansies or just a little advice, you know where to go. Thank you, Covington's, for helping Rowlett grow.
